As part of the sub-date, the committee resolved that the amalgamated transit union
615 ATU and the Saskatoon Transit meet to discuss options to enhance the de-escalation training offered.
Saskatoon Transit has developed an in-house training program for operators called Transit Interaction based on a similar program by O.C.
Transport in Ottawa.
The two-day course focuses on several topics including de-escalation, customer service, diversity and inclusion and current policies and procedures.
Operators are scheduled to attend the training at least once every three years.
In April 2021, Saskatoon Transit Management and ATU met to discuss potential improvements to the Transit Interaction program.
As part of these discussions, two enhancements were identified.
First, inclusion of actual incidents experienced by Saskatoon Transit operators.
The current training uses videos from third-party sources to illustrate issues and situations that may occur.
Using actual incidents experienced by Saskatoon Transit operators better connects the operators to situations that can and have occurred in Saskatoon
and better illustrates the incidents that can occur and how to respond to de-escalate these types of actual incidents.
And secondly, a more active role for driver trainers.
Saskatoon Transit uses a pool of driver trainers to deliver most training programs to operators.

By adding a driver trainer to the group of participants, additional peer support can be provided to strengthen the importance of following fair and rural enforcement policies and incident response and de-escalation protocol.
Saskatoon Transit Management closely tracks and monitors assaults a negative interactions with operators.

Training can be revised, additional areas of training can be added, or the frequency of training could be increased to provide further de-escalation training and support if the monitor of interactions deems necessary.
There are no budget implications for the two enhancements to the Transit Interaction program and the report also includes financial implications to provide an additional training de-escalate.
